description: A key the operator typed that matches nothing: the ELSE at app/cbl/COUSR00C.cbl:220-222 anchors the browse on USRIDINI, and STARTBR answers DFHRESP(NOTFND) at :600-606 over a file that does hold records. USRIDINI is ZZZZZZZZ, and the value is derived rather than picked: the highest key the seed carries is USER0005 and 'Z' sorts after 'U', so ZZZZZZZZ is strictly greater than every one of the ten keys and the greater-than-or-equal positioning of :588-595 can find no key at or after it. GTEQ is inside a COBOL comment at :592, which selects exactly the behaviour it would have requested, because GTEQ is the default of EXEC CICS STARTBR when neither GTEQ nor EQUAL is given - and this case would land on the same arm under either reading, since no key EQUALS ZZZZZZZZ either. That is what separates it from its four neighbours: case04 reaches the same arm because the file holds no record at all, case10 reaches it on the HIGH-VALUES sentinel of :263, case18 types a key that IS found, and case19 forces the WHEN OTHER arm of :607-613. Only here does an ordinary eight-character key sort past the end of a populated file, which is also the one shape that makes the browse scan for a row and come back empty rather than be refused a relation. THE ARM RAISES NO ERROR FLAG, AND THAT IS THE POINT (practice B5). :600-606 sets USER-SEC-EOF, moves 'You are at the top of the page...' to WS-MESSAGE, moves -1 to USRIDINL and sends the map, and it never touches WS-ERR-FLG - unlike :609, which does. ERR-FLG-OFF therefore still holds when control returns to PROCESS-PAGE-FORWARD, :286's IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON is true, and the whole rest of the paragraph runs with the end-of-file flag already set. Preserved, not repaired: :288's guard is false because EIBAID is DFHENTER, so no look-ahead READNEXT is issued; :292's guard is false because the file is at end, so INITIALIZE-USER-DATA never runs; :298 moves 1 to WS-IDX and the loop at :300 exits on its first test, so not one READNEXT is issued anywhere on this path; :308 is false, so the ELSE at :317-322 sets NEXT-PAGE-NO and then finds WS-IDX still 1, so the short-page increment at :320-321 must NOT fire and the count stays the 0 that :227 moved in. Pinning an increment that does not happen is this case's half of gate G28, and it is pinned twice: CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM is 00000000 in the navigation and PAGENUM is the eight-character 00000000 on the screen, never 00000001. ENDBR at :325 is still issued, because :325 was reached by falling through rather than by branching away. CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST and CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST are untouched: they are written only by :389 and :435 inside POPULATE-USER-DATA, which no row ever reached. THE CONTEXT IS 1, AND IT HAS TO BE. A typed key can only arrive through the RECEIVE at :121, which is in the ELSE of :115; on a first entry :117 MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COUSR0AO blanks the map - and app/cpy-bms/COUSR00.CPY:373 declares 01 COUSR0AO REDEFINES COUSR0AI, so both views are one storage and USRIDINI is blanked with it. A first entry therefore always lists from the top of the file and can never reach :221, which is why this case is a re-entry with EIBAID DFHENTER, exactly as case18 is. The same REDEFINES is why POPULATE-USER-DATA and :327 move into xxxI items and the sent map shows them. ROWS ARE SPACES, NOT LOW-VALUES, and the distinction is the case's own: :117 never ran, so nothing was blanked to low values, and INITIALIZE-USER-DATA never ran, so nothing was blanked to spaces either. Every one of the forty row items and the ten SEL cells is simply what :121's RECEIVE delivered - a payload that named none of them, so each arrives at its declared width in spaces - and the ten SEL cells being blank is also why the ordered EVALUATE TRUE at :151-185 falls to its WHEN OTHER and :183-184 blank both selection fields. ONE TRANSMISSION IS PINNED, THOUGH THE PARAGRAPHS SEND TWICE. SEND-USRLST-SCREEN is performed at :606 and again at :329 - :119 belongs to the first-entry branch and is not on this path - and the two differ, because :327 and :328 fall between them: the first still carries the spaces the RECEIVE left in PAGENUM and the ZZZZZZZZ it left in USRIDIN, the second carries 00000000 and blanks. A terminal would receive both and be left displaying the second, and the REST projection answers with that same last screen, so the contract pins the transmission the operator ends up looking at. expectedMessages is empty for the same reason it is empty in case04: it carries DISPLAY lines, the NOTFND arm has none, and the three DISPLAY sites at :608, :642 and :676 are all WHEN OTHER arms this case never reaches. expectedReturnCode is 0, as it is for all twenty: no path moves anything to RETURN-CODE and none calls CEE3ABD. USRSEC IS UNCHANGED, AND THAT IS AN ASSERTION. The screen browses and writes nothing, so expectedWrites is empty and all ten rows are pinned both field by field - the six app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy spans in declaration order, with SEC-USR-FILLER named because :23 names it - and as whole eighty-byte images, so the values, the total width and the filler having been emitted as spaces rather than zeros are all covered (gates G19, G21); expectedDatasets then adds what no row expectation can, that the file still holds exactly ten records at that width. SEED: app/data/ASCII holds nine fixtures and none is a security-user file, so USRSEC is seeded inline, and these ten rows are the in-stream records of app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 verbatim at their in-stream width of exactly 57 characters, none synthesized. No row is pre-padded here: the 23-byte shortfall is the absent SEC-USR-FILLER and it is carried to 80 once, at seed time, by the single USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 normalisation declared below, whose owners are the harness and FieldDiffer. The 80 is fixed independently by :48 DCB=(LRECL=80,RECFM=FB) and by :64-66 DEFINE CLUSTER KEYS(8,0) RECORDSIZE(80,80). SEC-USR-PWD stays the plaintext eight-character literal the legacy design stores and compares (practice B6); masking or omitting it would change what this contract asserts, and app/cpy-bms/COUSR00.CPY has no field for it, which is why it appears in every record image and in no screen field. CONVENTIONS, all inherited from case01 (practice B8): jobParameters is omitted rather than empty, because COUSR00C is no batch job and ParityCase refuses a job parameter for any unitKind but BATCH_JOB, so the three conversation scalars travel as screenRequest.eibcalen, screenRequest.aid and screenRequest.commarea['CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT'] - which is also how gate G37 and rule R6 are met, no server-side state existing anywhere on the path. eibcalen is 194 because app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy sums to 160 and the CDEMO-CU00-INFO extension of :67-75 is 8+8+8+1+1+8 = 34; COTRN00C's equivalent is 58 and must not be copied here. The extension arrives carrying nothing - the commarea names only the program context, so the two anchors and the selection fields arrive blank, the count arrives 0 and CDEMO-CU00-NEXT-PAGE-FLG arrives as the VALUE 'N' it is declared with at :71 - which is what a fresh search typed on the list screen looks like. The code page is named US-ASCII explicitly and never defaulted. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34, the source's own version stamp at :694 rather than an invented instant, because POPULATE-HEADER-INFO calls FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE at :564 on every send and two sends of an unpinned header would flap this gate (practice B7). USRSEC is addressed by its binding key throughout and never by a dataset name (gate G46). Page size ten is BEHAVIOUR, not configuration (gate G39): it is hard-coded at :293, :300, :347 and :352 and by 02 USER-REC OCCURS 10 TIMES at :57, and it appears nowhere in this file as a tunable - this page happens to show none of its ten rows, which is a different statement about the same ten. No attribute is declared, because COUSR00C moves none: it copies DFHBMSCA but not DFHATTR, it validates no individual field, and app/bms/COUSR00.bms:449-450 gives ERRMSG COLOR=RED statically - inventing a DFHRED move would be new behaviour. RULE R1: the plan mandates the class name UserMenuController, but the Function header at app/cbl/COUSR00C.cbl:5 reads 'List all users from USRSEC file', app/bms/COUSR00.bms paints 'List Users', and README.md:228 records CU00 the same way. The name comes from the plan and the behaviour from the source: this is a paginated list screen, and nothing here expects menu-shaped behaviour. The dead WS-USER-DATA array at :56-64 stays unmodelled, having no consumer (practice B5). PROVENANCE (practice B12, risk R-A): every expected value here was DERIVED BY STRUCTURED READING of the COBOL and its copybooks and was NOT captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy program - executing it is impossible in this environment, which has no z/OS or CICS runtime, whose COBOL compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, and which is missing the IBM-supplied DFHAID and DFHBMSCA. Only the provenance of the expected values is substituted; the twenty cases, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-of-zero gate all stand. The derivation rests on app/cbl/COUSR00C.cbl:56-75, :98-144, :149-232, :282-331, :384-441, :446-501, :522-544 and :562-581, and on :218-222, :286-296, :317-323, :325-329 and :600-606 in particular; on app/cpy-bms/COUSR00.CPY, whose xxxI items give every payload name and width while its xxxL, xxxF and xxxA items stay metadata; on app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23, whose 8+20+20+8+1 = 57 plus the named SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) make 80; on app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:18-22 for the two forty-character titles; and on app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:88-99, which defines FILE(USRSEC) with ADD, BROWSE, DELETE, READ and UPDATE, of which this program uses browse alone.
